context: Data visualization — arc diagram showing character co-occurrence relationships in a synthetic novel, with 30 nodes ordered by first appearance and ~90 edges encoded by arc height and stroke width
first_impression: Intentionally designed with a muted Tol palette and deliberate encodings, but the dense arc tangle in the middle third of the canvas overwhelms readability in the static view
what_works: Palette choice (Tol muted, explicitly named) avoids schemeCategory10 defaults and produces a coherent, restrained color story. The weight legend using actual mini-arcs is clever and on-brand.
what_doesnt: The upper ~40% of the SVG is dead space — arcs only fill the lower portion, making the chart feel bottom-heavy and wasteful. With 90 edges at low opacity, the static view reads as visual noise; the design only resolves on hover, meaning the first impression penalizes the chart despite the thoughtful interaction.
